provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The rule (find plus/diamond centres = background cells whose four orthogonal neighbours are the plus colour; connect consecutive centres sharing a row with a horizontal line from centre+2 to next centre-2, and likewise along columns) treats rows and columns symmetrically and is direction-free, so it is invariant under every D4 transform: the emitted program operates directly on the visible grid with no orientation change needed. Colour roles are specialised through the palette: background = palette[0], plus colour = palette[2], connecting line colour = palette[1]. Lines only overwrite background cells, matching the generator, where plusses are drawn after the lines and so a perpendicular plus's tip lying on a connecting line stays the plus colour. Connecting only consecutive centres is equivalent to the generator's all-pairs drawing, because intermediate plusses are redrawn on top of those lines.
draft_notes.limitations: Relies on the generator's guarantees: plus bounding boxes do not overlap or touch, so no false centres appear, and all centres are interior. If two plusses on one line were closer than four cells apart (impossible in this domain), no line would be drawn between them. The archived solver overwrites any cell between tips with the line colour. This program instead preserves plus-colour tip cells from unrelated plusses, as the generator does. The two can only differ in scenes where a line crosses a perpendicular plus's tip. Untested.
